85.subject: Botany
85.text: Which part of the world has a high density of organism?
85.sol: Tropical rain forests are mainly found in central America, along Amazon and Orinoco rivers, South America, Congo river basin of Africa, Malagasy Republic and South east Asia including India. Diversity of life is so high that a hectare of the forest may have as many as 200 species of trees, (70 %-80 % ) of all insects and (80-85 % ) of all birds are known from tropical forests. Productivity of this biome is also very high and life is abundant. It has different varieties and number of plants and animals.

71238.text: How many electrons and ATP are required for the biological fixation of a molecule of nitrogen to form ammonia?

72374.subject: Physics
72374.text: The potential barrier in p-n junction diode is due to
options: depletion of positive charges near the junction.
accumulation of positive charges near the junction.
depletion of negative charges near the the junction.
accumulation of positive and negative charges near the junction.
72374.sol: When a p-n junction is formed, majority charge carriers diffuse across the junction due to the concentration gradient. Electrons from the n-region diffuse into the p-region, leaving behind immobile positively charged donor ions. Similarly, holes from the p-region diffuse into the n-region, leaving behind immobile negatively charged acceptor ions. options: Viruses are "non-living" entities but it can interact with antibiotics

74216.sol: Antibiotics work by changing or altering any important metabolic pathway in bacteria. Different types of antibiotics act on different pathways to kill or inhibit bacterial growth. 80061.subject: Botany
options: the main axis terminates in a flower

80061.sol: In racemose inflorescence, the main axis continues to grow indefinitely and does not terminate in a flower. The flowers are borne laterally in an acropetal succession, meaning the older flowers are at the base and the younger flowers or buds are at the apex. In cymose inflorescence, the main axis terminates in a flower, hence its growth is limited, and the flowers are borne in a basipetal order. Answer: flowers are borne in an acropetal succession

84444.text: Neoplastic characteristics of cells refer to : A. A mass of proliferating cell B. Rapid growth of cells C. Invasion and damage to the surrounding tissue D. Those confined to original location Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
84444.sol: The correct answer will include : A, B and C only. A neoplasm is a general term for any abnormal growth of tissue. Neoplastic characteristics of cells refer to (1) A mass of proliferating cell. (2) Rapid growth of cells. (3) Invasion and damage to the surrounding tissue. Cancer specifically refers to malignant neoplasms, which are cancerous and invasive. Benign tumours remain confined to their original location. Thus, D is not included in the answer. The malignant tumours, on the other hand are a mass of proliferat

84446.subject: Zoology
84446.text: After maturation, in primary lymphoid organs, the lymphocytes migrate for interaction with antigens to secondary lymphoid organ(s) / tissue(s) like A. thymus B. bone marrow C. spleen D. lymph nodes E. Peyer's patches Choose the correct answer from the options given below
84446.sol: The primary lymphoid organs are bone marrow and thymus where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes. After maturation, the lymphocytes migrate into secondary lymphoid organs like spleen, lymph nodes, Peyer's patches of small intestine and appendix. These secondary lymphoid organ provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen.

84450.subject: Zoology
84450.text: Which of the following sexually transmitted infections are completely curable?
84450.sol: Option (4) is the answer because, genital warts, trichomoniasis and syphilis are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. Hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections are not completely curable.

84545.subject: Zoology
84545.text: Common cold is not cured by antibiotics because it is
options: caused by a Gram positive bacterium
caused by a Gram negative bacterium
84545.sol: Common cold is not cured by antibiotics because it is caused by a virus, called rhinovirus.

84629.subject: Zoology
84629.text: In human females, meiosis-II is not completed until?
84629.sol: In human females, meiosis-II is completed after the entry of sperm into the cytoplasm of the secondary oocyte at the time of fertilization leading to the formation of ovum and secondary polar body.

84632.subject: Zoology
84632.text: Which of the following cells during gametogenesis is normally diploid?
84632.sol: Spermatogonia or the sperm mother cell is diploid while all other cells are formed as a result of meiotic division and hense are haploid in nature.

84854.subject: Zoology
84854.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : DNA polymerases catalyse polymerisation only in one direction, that is 5^ 3^ Statement II : During replication of DNA, on one strand the replication is continuous while on other strand it is discontinuous. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
84854.sol: DNA polymerase can read template DNA in only one direction i.e., 3^ 5^ thus DNA replication can continue only in 5^ 3^ direction, thus it can continue only on one strand of DNA. The DNA stand on which replication is continuous is called leading strand whereas the strand on which replication is discontinuous is said to be lagging strand.

84868.subject: Zoology
84868.text: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions in DNA sequence, called as:
84868.sol: DNA fingerprinting is a very quick way to compare the DNA sequences of any two individuals. DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions in a DNA sequence called repetitive DNA because, in these sequences, a small stretch of DNA is repeated many times.

84937.subject: Zoology
84937.text: Read the following four statement. I. In transcription, adenosine pairs with uracil. II. Regulation of lac operon by repressor is referred to as positive regulation. III. The human genome has approximately 50000 genes. IV. Haemophilia is a sex-linked recessive disease. How many of the above statements are right?
84937.sol: Transcription is the process of synthesis of RNA on the DNA template. During transcription adenosine pairs with uracil. Repressor gene determines the transcription of structural gene. It codes for repressor protein. After synthesis the repressor molecule is diffused from the ribosome and bind to the operator in absence of inducer. The human genome has approximately 30000 genes with 3.2 billion base pairs.

84983.subject: Zoology
84983.text: Which one of the following pairs of nitrogenous bases of nucleic acids, is wrongly matched with the category mentioned against it?
84983.sol: Adenine and guanine are purines, whereas, Uracil, Thymine, Cytosine are pyrimidines.

85345.subject: Zoology
85345.text: Change in the sequence of nucleotide in DNA is called as:
85345.sol: A mutation is a change in a DNA sequence. Mutations can result from DNA copying mistakes made during cell division, exposure to ionizing radiation, exposure to chemicals called mutagens, or infection by viruses. Related Theory:- Chromosome mutation is the process of change that results in rearranged chromosome parts, abnormal numbers of individual chromosomes, or abnormal numbers of chromosome sets.

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
100343.sol: Assertion (A) is true: When the lift is accelerating upwards with acceleration a , the relative acceleration of the ball with respect to the lift is a_ rel = g - (-a) = g + a (downwards). Since the effective acceleration (g + a) is greater than g , the time taken to hit the floor t = 2h g+a is less than the time taken in a stationary lift t = 2h g . 100581.subject: Physics
100581.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R Assertion A : An electric fan continues to rotate for some time after the current is switched off. Reason R : Fan continues to rotate due to inertia of motion. In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
100581.sol: When a fan is rotating, it acquires some kinetic energy. When the switch is off, because of its motion, it continues rotating for some time until it stops because of the air friction. So it is due to inertia of motion that fan continues to rotate. Hence, both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A .

When found attached to a sugar, they are called nucleosides. If a phosphate group is also found esterified to the sugar they are called nucleotides. Adenosine, guanosine, thymidine, uridine and cytidine are nucleosides. Adenylic acid, thymidylic acid, guanylic acid, uridylic acid and cytidylic acid are nucleotides.

126995.subject: Botany
126995.text: A scrubber in the exhaust of a chemical industrial plant removes:
options: Particulate matter of the size 5 micrometer or above
Particulate matter of the size 2.5 micrometer or less
126995.sol: A scrubber can remove gases like sulphur dioxide. In a scrubber, the exhaust is passed through a spray of water or lime. Sulphur dioxide is a major pollutant of chemical industrial plants and the dry scrubbing method is mainly used to remove this pollution.

127403.subject: Botany
127403.text: Read the following statements regarding alien species invasions: (A) The introduction of Nile perch into Lake Victoria in East Africa led to the extinction of more than 200 species of cichlid fish. (B) Carrot grass (Parthenium), Lantana and water hyacinth (Eichhornia) are invasive weed species that pose a threat to native species in India. (C) The illegal introduction of the African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) for a
127403.sol: Statement (A) is correct. The introduction of the Nile perch into Lake Victoria eventually led to the extinction of an ecologically unique assemblage of more than 200 species of cichlid fish. Statement (B) is correct. Parthenium, Lantana, and Eichhornia are well-known invasive weed species that cause environmental damage and threaten native species. Statement (C) is correct. The African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) was illegally introduced for aquaculture and threatens indigenous catfishes. Statement (D) is incorre

127573.subject: Botany
127573.text: What is secondary productivity in an ecosystem?
options: The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis
The rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers
127573.sol: A constant input of solar energy is the basic requirement for any ecosystem to function and sustain. Primary production is defined as the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. It is expressed in terms of weight (g m–2) or energy (kcal m–2). The rate of biomass production is called productivity. It is expressed in terms of gm–2 yr –1 or (kcal m–2) yr–1 to compare the productivity of different ecosystems. It can be divided into gross primary pro

128824.subject: Zoology
128824.text: What is the purpose of blood coagulation?
128824.sol: Blood exhibits coagulation or clotting in response to an injury or trauma. This is a mechanism to prevent excessive loss of blood from the body . You would have observed a dark reddish brown scum formed at the site of a cut or an injury over a period of time. It is a clot or coagulam formed mainly of a network of threads called fibrins in which dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped. Fibrins are formed by the conversion of inactive fibrinogens in the plasma by the enzyme thrombin. Thrombins, in turn

128913.subject: Zoology
128913.text: What does the T-wave represent in an ECG?
128913.sol: The P-wave represents the electrical excitation (or depolarisation) of the atria, which leads to the contraction of both the atria. The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles, which initiates the ventricular contraction. The contraction starts shortly after Q and marks the beginning of the systole. The T-wave represents the return of the ventricles from excited to normal state (repolarisation) . The end of the T-wave marks the end of systole. Obviously, by counting the number of QRS complexes t

128970.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Protein albumin help in osmotic balance. Reason: Plasma without the clotting factors is called serum.

Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128970.sol: Protein albumin help in osmotic balance. Plasma without the clotting factors is called serum.

129101.text: Identify the given figure and select the correct option.

Eosinophil - their number increases during allergic infection.
Lymphocyte - small sized non-motile and non-phagocytic.
Monocyte - motile and phagocytic in nature.
129101.sol: Neutrophil is a phagocytic cell which destroys foreign organisms entering the body. It has many lobed nucleus, fine granules in cytoplasm and it takes acidic as well as basic stains.

129470.subject: Zoology
129470.text: What type of excretory structures are found in most vertebrates?
129470.sol: A survey of animal kingdom presents a variety of excretory structures. In most of the invertebrates, these structures are simple tubular forms whereas vertebrates have complex tubular organs called kidneys. Some of these structures are mentioned here. Protonephridia or flame cells are the excretory structures in Platyhelminthes (Flatworms, e.g., Planaria), rotifers, some annelids and the cephalochordate – Amphioxus. Protonephridia are primarily concerned with ionic and fluid volume regulation, i.e., osmoregulation.

130030.subject: Zoology
130030.text: ___ is a pathological condition wherein the body on the whole or a part of the body is not supplied with sufficient oxygen.
130030.sol: hypoxia is a pathological condition wherein the body on the whole or a part of the body is not supplied with sufficient oxygen.

130053.sol: A major percentage (97%) of O₂ is transported by RBCs in the blood, and the remaining percentage (3%) of O₂ is transported through plasma.

130581.subject: Zoology
130581.text: How long do females need to take oral contraceptive pills each cycle?
130581.sol: Oral administration of small doses of either progestogens or progestogen–estrogen combinations is another contraceptive method used by the females. They are used in the form of tablets and hence are popularly called the pills. Pills have to be taken daily for a period of 21 days starting preferably within the first five days of menstrual cycle. After a gap of 7 days (during which menstruation occurs) it has to be repeated in the same pattern till the female desires to prevent conception. They inhibit ovulation and

130793.subject: Zoology
130793.text: A married couple seeks medical help for infertility. Clinical evaluation reveals that the female partner has normal, patent fallopian tubes and a normal uterus, but her ovaries fail to produce viable ova. The male partner has a normal sperm count and normal sperm motility. Which of the following Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) is the most suitable for this couple?
130793.sol: The female partner cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment for fertilization and further embryonic development, as her fallopian tubes and uterus are normal. The male partner has normal sperm parameters. In such cases, the most suitable technique is GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer). An ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of the female, allowing in-vivo fertilization by the male partner's sperms. ZIFT and ICSI involve in-vitro fertilization, which is unnecessary

130859.subject: Zoology
130859.text: What is the function of the oviducts in the female reproductive system?
options: Transport of ovum from ovary to uterus
130859.sol: The oviducts (fallopian tubes), uterus and vagina constitute the female accessory ducts. Each fallopian tube is about 10-12 cm long and extends from the periphery of each ovary to the uterus, the part closer to the ovary is the funnel-shaped infundibulum. The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriae, which help in collection of the ovum after ovulation. The infundibulum leads to a wider part of the oviduct called ampulla. The last part of the oviduct, isthmus has a narrow lumen and

130886.text: What does the head of a sperm contain?
options: The head of a sperm contains a diploid nucleus
The head of a sperm contains a haploid nucleus covered by a cap-like structure, the acrosome
The head of a sperm contains numerous mitochondria
The head of a sperm contains enzymes that help fertilization
130886.sol: It is a microscopic structure composed of a head, neck, a middle piece and a tail. A plasma membrane envelops the whole body of sperm. The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, the anterior portion of which is covered by a cap-like structure, acrosome . The acrosome is filled with enzymes that help fertilisation of the ovum. The middle piece possesses numerous mitochondria, which produce energy for the movement of tail that facilitate sperm motility essential for fertilisation. The human male ejaculates

131110.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. Fertilization can only occur if the ovum and sperms are transported simultaneously to the ampullary region. 2. The process of fusion of a sperm with an ovum is called fertilization. 3. The secretions of the acrosome help the sperm enter into the Cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane. 4. During fertilisation, a sperm com
131110.sol: Fertilization can only occur if the ovum and sperms are transported simultaneously to the ampullary region. The process of fusion of a sperm with an ovum is called fertilization. The secretions of the acrosome help the sperm enter into the Cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane.

131166.subject: Zoology
131166.text: What is the function of corpus luteum?
131166.sol: The corpus luteum secretes the hormone progesterone

131439.sol: The beads-on-string structure in chromatin is packaged to form chromatin fibers that are further coiled and condensed at the metaphase stage of cell division to form chromosomes. The packaging of chromatin at higher levels requires an additional set of proteins that collectively are referred to as Non-histone Chromosomal (NHC) proteins. 132259.text: Under what condition would a daughter be color blind according to the paragraph?

If her mother is a carrier and her father is color blind
If both her parents are carriers
If her mother is color blind and her father is normal
132259.sol: It is a sex-linked recessive disorder due to defect in either red or green cone of eye resulting in failure to discriminate between red and green colour. This defect is due to mutation in certain genes present in the X chromosome. It occurs in about 8 per cent of males and only about 0.4 per cent of females. This is because the genes that lead to red-green colour blindness are on the X chromosome. Males have only one X chromosome and females have two. The son of a woman who carries the gene has a 50 per cent chance

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
132429.sol: Thalassemia and sickle-cell anaemia are both autosomal recessive blood disorders. According to NCERT, Thalassemia differs from sickle-cell anaemia in that the former is a quantitative problem of synthesising too few globin molecules, while the latter is a qualitative problem of synthesising an incorrectly functioning globin. If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
132535.sol: Haemophilia is a X-linked disease. As a person receives X chromosome from mother and Y from father, therefore the person may be a haemophilic if his mother is carrier of the disease. The person will be certainly haemophilic if his mother is haemophilic.

132644.subject: Zoology
132644.text: A person who is trisomic for twenty first pair of chromosome suffers from
132644.sol: Down's syndrome (45+ XX or 45+ XY ) is the case when there is one extra chromosome in 21st pair of autosome. It is also called trisomy 21 or trisomy-G. It is most common in children of over aged mothers (above 41 years). It is also called Mongolian syndrome.

132679.subject: Zoology
132679.text: What is the significance of studying extinct organisms, such as dinosaurs, through fossils?
options: They help understand the present climate
They provide insight into past life-forms and evolutionary changes
They show current life-forms’ similarities to ancient ones
132679.sol: Fossils in various layers indicate that certain life-forms are restricted to specific geological periods, showing changes over time.A study of fossils in different sedimentary layers indicates the geological period in which they existed. The study showed that life-forms varied over time and certain life forms are restricted to certain geological time- spans. Hence, new forms of life have arisen at different times in the history of earth. All this is called paleontological evidence. Studying extinct organisms like d

133019.subject: Zoology
133019.text: Variation in gene frequencies within populations can occur by chance rather than by natural selection. This is referred to as
133019.sol: Genetic drift is a random change in allele frequencies over the generations. It is brought by chance alone. Gene flow or gene migration is the physical movement of alleles into and out of a population. The existence within the population of disadvantages alleles in heterozygous genotypes is known as genetic code.

Erythroxylum coca yields cocaine, which interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine. 134470.text: What is the ability of plasmids and bacteriophages in bacterial cells?
options: Replicating within control of chromosomal DNA
Replicating independently of the control of chromosomal DNA
Replicating with control of chromosomal DNA
134470.sol: You know that plasmids and bacteriophages have the ability to replicate within bacterial cells independent of the control of chromosomal DNA . Bacteriophages because of their high number per cell, have very high copy numbers of their genome within the bacterial cells. Some plasmids may have only one or two copies per cell whereas others may have >15-100 copies per cell. Their numbers can go even higher. If we are able to link an alien piece of DNA with bacteriophage or plasmid DNA, we can multiply its numbers equal

134497.subject: Zoology
134497.text: What type of virus has the ability to transform normal cells into cancerous cells?
134497.sol: Similarly, retroviruses in animals have the ability to transform normal cells into cancerous cells . A better understanding of the art of delivering genes by pathogens in their eukaryotic hosts has generated knowledge to transform these tools of pathogens into useful vectors for delivering genes of interest to humans. The tumor inducing (Ti) plasmid of Agrobacterium tumifaciens has now been modified into a cloning vector which is no more pathogenic to the plants but is still able to use the mechanisms to deliver ge

134558.subject: Zoology
134558.text: What is a bioreactor in the context of biotechnology?
options: A vessel in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products, individual enzymes, etc usi
A vessel in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products, individual enzymes, etc usi
A vessel in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products, individual enzymes, etc usi
A vessel in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products, individual enzymes, etc usi
134558.sol: To produce in large quantities, the development of bioreactors, where large volumes (100-1000 litres) of culture can be processed, was required. Thus, bioreactors can be thought of as ves sels in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific prod ucts, individual enzymes, etc., using microbial plant, animal or human cells . A bioreactor provides the optimal conditions for achieving the desired product by providing optimum growth conditions (temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins, oxygen).

134859.text: A genetic engineer is attempting to introduce a human gene into the plasmid vector pBR322. If the human DNA fragment was isolated by digesting the human genome with the restriction enzyme BamH I, which of the following enzymes must be used to cleave the pBR322 plasmid to ensure successful ligation?
134859.sol: For a recombinant DNA molecule to be created, both the source DNA (human gene) and the vector DNA (pBR322) must be cut with the same restriction endonuclease. Using the same restriction enzyme ensures that both DNA molecules have complementary sticky ends, which can then be joined by the enzyme DNA ligase. Since the human DNA was cut with BamH I, the pBR322 plasmid must also be cut with BamH I. 6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a1b.subject: Biology
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a1b.text: Two species of herbivorous mammals inhabit the same savanna and rely on similar vegetation for food. To avoid competitive exclusion and successfully coexist in the same habitat, these species are most likely to:
options: synchronize their grazing schedules to feed simultaneously.
partition their resources by grazing on different parts of the plants.
increase their reproductive rate to aggressively outnumber the other species.
develop a predator-prey relationship with each other.
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a1b.sol: According to Gause's competitive exclusion principle, two species competing for the exact same resources cannot stably coexist. To avoid competitive exclusion and coexist in the same habitat, competing species often evolve to utilize different aspects of the shared resource, a process known as resource partitioning. By grazing on different parts of the plants (for example, one species eating the tall stems while the other eats the lower leaves), the two herbivorous mammal species reduce direct competition, allowing

6a2a77befad2360f42564bbd.subject: Chemistry
6a2a77befad2360f42564bbd.text: In a particular thermodynamic process, a gas releases 250 J of heat to its surroundings while 600 J of work is done on it. What is the change in internal energy of the gas?
6a2a77befad2360f42564bbd.sol: According to the first law of thermodynamics: Q = U + W Since heat is released by the gas to the surroundings, Q = -250 J. Since work is done on the gas, W = -600 J. Substituting these values into the first law equation: -250 = U - 600 U = 600 - 250 = +350 J Answer: +350 J

6a13e467688ac6d0667aad42.subject: Chemistry
6a13e467688ac6d0667aad42.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Nucleotides are joined together by phosphodiester linkage between 5' and 3' carbon atoms of the pentose sugar. Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

95696.subject: Botany
95696.text: Lichens are symbiotic association between two organisms. Which of these statements about them is true?
options: Lichens are fast growing organisms that live for a short period
The algal component is called mycobiont and fungal component is called phycobiont
They are pioneers of vegetation on rocks.
95696.sol: Lichens are symbiotic associations between algae and fungi. The autotrophic algal component is called phycobiont and the heterotrophic fungal component is called as mycobiont. Algae prepare food for fungi and fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for its partner. Lichens are very good pollution indicators - they do not grow in polluted areas and in cities. Lichens are pioneers in the xerosere type of ecological succession on barren rocks.

96511.subject: Botany
96511.text: Which of the following statements regarding food chain is false?
options: In an aquatic ecosystem, grazing food chain is the major conduit for energy flow.
In terrestrial ecosystems, a large fraction of energy flows through detritus food chain.
The detritus food chain begins with dead organic matter.
Primary consumers belong to the first trophic level.
96511.sol: All animals depend on plants directly or indirectly for their food needs. They are hence, called consumers and also heterotrophs. If they feed on the producer, the plants (belonging to the first trophic level), they are called primary consumers. Obviously the primary consumers will be herbivores. Some common herbivores are insects, birds and mammals in terrestrial ecosystem and molluscs in aquatic system. Thus, primary consumers belong to the second trophic level.

96595.subject: Botany
96595.text: The trees occupy the top vertical strata of a forest, shrubs the second and herbs and grasses occupy the bottom layers, this represents
96595.sol: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called stratification. For example, trees occupy top vertical strata or layers of a forest, shrubs the second and herbs and grasses occupy the bottom layers.

97625.text: In aerobic respiration, how many times more ATP is produced than anaerobic respiration?
97625.sol: In aerobic respiration during complete oxidation of one glucose molecule, 38 ATP are produced. However, in anaerobic respiration, only 2 ATP are produced. Thus, in aerobic respiration, 19 times more ATP is produced than in anaerobic respiration.

Panther and Felis domestica are placed in different families.
97804.sol: Potato and brinjal not only belongs to the same family but also to the same genus i.e. Solanum . The scientific name of potato and brinjal is Solanum tuberosum and Solanum melongena respectively. Felis and Canis belong to a different families.

98154.subject: Chemistry
98154.text: Statement 1 - Competitive inhibitor is also called as substrate analogue. Statement 2 - It resembles the enzyme in structure.
98154.sol: In competitive inhibition, an inhibitor that resembles the normal substrate binds to the enzyme, usually at the active site, and prevents the substrate from binding. At any given moment, the enzyme may be bound to the inhibitor, the substrate, or neither, but it cannot bind to both at the same time.

306824.text: Which among the following are electromagnetic waves?

6a7a1ff8b127302f4a32d292.sol: The orbital speed of a satellite is given by v = GM r , where M is the mass of the planet and r is the orbital radius. Since both satellites have the same orbital speed, their orbital radii r must be equal. The time period of revolution is T = 2 r v . Since both r and v are identical for the two satellites, their time periods must also be equal. 6a7a1ff8db9defb2e78cc486.text: The root mean square (r.m.s) speed of the molecules of a rigid diatomic gas is 600 m s ⁻¹ . If the molar mass of the gas is 30 g mol ⁻¹ , the internal energy of one mole of this gas is
6a7a1ff8db9defb2e78cc486.sol: The root mean square speed of a gas is given by: v_ rms = 3RT M Squaring and rearranging for RT gives: RT = M v_ rms ^2 3 For a rigid diatomic gas, the internal energy of one mole is: U = 5 2 RT Substituting the expression for RT into the internal energy equation: U = 5 2 ( M v_ rms ^2 3 ) = 5 6 M v_ rms ^2 The molar mass must be converted to SI units: M = 30 g mol ⁻¹ = 0.03 kg mol ⁻¹ Now, substitute the given values: U = 5 6 0.03 (600)^2 U = 5 6 0.03 360000 U = 5 0.005 360000 = 9000 J . Answer: 9000 J

6a7a1ff8096d3d9ccae1d3d1.text: A Zener diode with a breakdown voltage of 10 V is used to regulate the voltage across a variable load resistor R_L . 6a7a1ff8096d3d9ccae1d3d1.sol: For the Zener diode to operate in the breakdown region, the voltage across the load terminals (with the Zener diode considered open-circuit) must be greater than or equal to the Zener breakdown voltage V_Z . Using the voltage divider rule, the open-circuit voltage V_ oc across R_L is: V_ oc = V_ in R_L R_s + R_L Setting the condition V_ oc V_Z : 30 R_L 400 + R_L 10 Dividing both sides by 10 : 3 R_L 400 + R_L 2 R_L 400 R_L 200 Thus, the minimum required value of the load resistance is 200 . Answer: 200
